title: From Spoon to Trophy, By Two Shots
title_candidates: From Spoon to Trophy, By Two Shots
theme: David Mullin, a three-time consecutive Wooden Spoon holder, becomes a double champion by a margin as thin as one bad hole for his closest rival — while the tournament's most historic single round belongs to the man who finished last.
opening_hook: Open in medias res on the 16th at Prince's in round four, Alex Baker still just two shots off the Trophy lead before he plays it, then cut back to explain how David Mullin — three-time reigning Wooden Spoon holder — built the cushion that survived it.

trophy_storyline.subject: David Mullin, coming off three straight Wooden Spoons, led the Trophy from round one to round four and held off a furious late rally from Alex Baker to win by two.
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: This is the report's central story: the champion's turnaround and the closest possible finish, decided by one calamitous hole for the runner-up.
trophy_storyline.shape: Mullin took the Trophy lead early in round one and was the best golfer in the field for the first two rounds, stretching his advantage to nine shots. He then fell into the bottom half of the field for rounds three and four, and Alex Baker outscored him in both, cutting the gap from nine down to two. Baker's charge was undone at the death by a sextuple-bogey 10 at the 16th — his second identical disaster of the week at that hole number — and Mullin held on to win by two.
headline_candidates: From Spoon to Trophy, By Two
Baker's Charge Falls One Hole Short
trophy_storyline.standfirst: A three-time Wooden Spoon holder turned Trophy champion held off a grandstand finish from Alex Baker, whose charge was undone by the same nightmare hole that had wrecked his tournament three rounds earlier.

jacket_storyline.subject: David Mullin's Green Jacket was built, not inherited — a lead he stretched to twelve shots and never seriously risked, even as the closing margin looked dramatic.
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Contrasts with the Trophy race: on Gross, Mullin was unambiguously the best player in the field all week, no rally required.
jacket_storyline.shape: Mullin led the Green Jacket from round one and extended it to twelve shots by the end of round three. In round four, Gregg Williams and Jon Baker each clawed back a big chunk of that lead — Williams from 18 down to 8, Baker from 15 down to 7 — but neither threatened the result. Mullin beat Jon Baker head-to-head in three of the four rounds and never finished worse than third in any single round.
headline_candidates: Twelve Down to Seven, Never in Doubt
Mullin's Cushion Survives a Final-Day Fright
The Jacket That Nearly Looked Close
jacket_storyline.chosen_headline: Twelve Down to Seven, Never in Doubt
jacket_storyline.standfirst: David Mullin's gross lead shrank by five shots in the final round alone, but the Green Jacket was never seriously threatened.

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker's Wooden Spoon was earned across two separate last-place rounds, not lost in a single afternoon.
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: Confirms the Spoon was built rather than gifted by others' misfortune — the least dramatic but most honest version of how last place is decided.
spoon_storyline.shape: Jon Baker was worst in the field in two of the four rounds, round one and round three, the second of those capped by a triple bogey at the 17th. A strong final round — eleven points better than his poor round three — arrived too late to matter, and he finished twelve shots adrift of Gregg Williams, the next worst.
headline_candidates: The Spoon Was Never in Doubt
spoon_storyline.standfirst: Jon Baker was worst in the field in two separate rounds, and the final one came a day too late to change anything.

discovered_storylines.subject: Jon Baker set a new Prince's course record and tied an all-time TEG streak record in the same round that confirmed his Wooden Spoon.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The tournament's single most historic round of golf belonged to the man who finished last overall — the sharpest irony of the week.
discovered_storylines.shape: Already resigned to the Wooden Spoon after three bottom-half rounds, Jon Baker went five holes without dropping a gross shot and piled up 14 points across holes 12-15 in round four, breaking the Prince's course record with an 83 (beating a mark that had stood across five prior visits) and tying the all-time TEG record for a two-hole birdie streak. He still found a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 18th before the round was out.
headline_candidates: Baker Breaks the Course Record — And Still Finishes Last
History and the Wooden Spoon, Same Afternoon
A Record for the Man Who Needed It Least
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Baker Breaks the Course Record — And Still Finishes Last
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A new Prince's course record and a share of the all-time TEG streak mark landed in the same round that sealed Jon Baker's Wooden Spoon.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker carded the exact same disaster score, at the same hole number, on two different courses, three rounds apart.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A genuine coincidence that bookends his tournament and explains two of his three heaviest score blows of the week.
discovered_storylines.shape: In round one at Royal Cinque Ports, Alex Baker carded a quintuple-bogey 10 at the 16th. Three rounds later, on the entirely different 16th at Prince's, the same number appeared again — this time a sextuple-bogey 10 that ended a steady run and cost him a share of the Trophy lead he was closing on.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Two different courses, the same hole number, and the same catastrophic 10 — bookending a tournament Alex Baker otherwise nearly won.

discovered_storylines.subject: Gregg Williams quietly posted his best-ever TEG gross total while never threatening the leaders.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: A personal-best round that deserves its own mention rather than being buried inside the Jacket arithmetic.
discovered_storylines.shape: Williams blew up early with a quadruple-bogey 9 at the 3rd in round one and trailed the Green Jacket by 18 shots at his worst point. He answered a poor round two with a strong round three, gradually clawing the gap back to 8, and finished with a personal-best gross total of +76.
headline_candidates: A Personal Best in the Shadows
discovered_storylines.standfirst: An 18-shot deficit after a blown-up third hole didn't stop Gregg Williams closing hard and posting his best-ever TEG gross total.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Mullin's run from three consecutive Wooden Spoons to Trophy champion is genuine and used as supporting historical framing behind the closer, hole-16 counterfactual finish.

why_the_champion_won: Mullin was the best golfer in the field for the first two rounds, building a nine-shot cushion, then simply survived as Alex Baker outscored him for the back two — Baker's grand rally arrived one hole too late, undone by his own second identical disaster at the 16th.
